validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: independently corroborated by two distinct-origin sources. (1) trademanegypt.com, an Egyptian piping/valve EPC subcontractor, lists 'Abu Sultan–Al Shabab Power Station Pipeline' as a completed project (Category: Power Generation; Client: Egyptian Natural Gas Company - GASCO; Year: 2021; Contractor: Petrojet) — live and verified (url_verifier OK, tokens 'Abu Sultan'/'Shabab'/'Gasco'/'Petrojet'/'2021' all present). (2) The GASCO national-grid map embedded in the EGAS Annual Report 2018 (page footer '35', PDF page 19) shows a GREEN ('Existing P/L' per the map legend) line running from a facility icon labeled 'EL Shabab' to the 'Abu Sultan' locality, explicitly labeled '24" 38 km' — an exact match to GEM's Diameter=24in and LengthKnown=38.00km. I verified this by rendering the PDF page to a 400dpi image and reading the map directly (pdftotext of this 22MB PDF does not surface 'Shabab' anywhere — the url_verifier tool's own documented caveat notes it does not reach the whole document on large PDFs, and per this batch's guidance a missed full-text hit on a report that primarily conveys this information via its map is not evidence of an unsupported citation). Both the icon at 'El Shabab' and a nearby icon at 'Abu Sultan' use the map legend's blue 'POWER STATION' symbol, consistent with trademanegypt's 'Power Station Pipeline' naming and 'Power Generation' category — GEM's EndPrefecture/District value 'El Shabab P.S.' should be read as 'El Shabab Power Station' for this row specifically (unlike the more common 'pressure station' reading noted elsewhere in this scope), which is itself accurate and needs no change. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is reasonable — the map places this line inside the 'NATURAL GAS NATIONAL GRID' network, the same categorization used for other GASCO trunk mains in this scope (e.g. P8021 Kuraimat–Al Tebbin, also a power-station supply line classified transmission); no reclassification warranted. DUPLICATE: checked against all 39 other in-scope rows — no other row references Abu Sultan+El Shabab or overlaps this corridor; not a match to the Trans-Sinai/Abr Sinai family (those run El-Tina–Sinai, a different corridor entirely) nor to the Ameriya-node cluster. No duplicate found. ATTRIBUTION: StartLocation=Abu Sultan / EndPrefecture=El Shabab P.S., both State/Province=Ismailia — both place names sit in the correct Ismailia-area region on the map (east of the Delta, west of the Suez Canal, near '10th of Ramadan'/'National Gas' distribution nodes), consistent with GEM's location fields. Fuel=Gas is well supported (client is Egypt's national GAS company and the line is drawn as part of the NATIONAL GAS grid map) — tier high, independent, for existence/fuel/classification/location. SPEC (length/diameter): the 24in/38km match is currently support by ONE primary-source document (the GASCO/EGAS map) read visually; trademanegypt does not give numeric specs, so I could not reach a second independently-sourced numeric confirmation this pass (WebSearch quota for the session was already exhausted at 200/200 before I could search further in English or Arabic — a fresh-session follow-up on Arabic-language GASCO/EGAS material could try to find a second numeric source). Overall tier reflects that gap.

validity.researcher_notes: GGIT_gas_snapshot_20260827.csv row for P8074 (SheetRow 4334) has StartYear1='' (blank) and StartMonth1='2021' — a bare 4-digit year is sitting in the MONTH field, not the year field; this is a mechanical column-mapping error, not a research finding. Separately, and more substantively: the '2021' figure traces to trademanegypt.com's project-card metadata (Client/Contractor/Year), but trademanegypt is a piping-and-valve EPC subcontractor whose portfolio year most plausibly records when THEIR scope of supply/contract closed — not necessarily the pipeline's original commissioning date. The EGAS Annual Report 2018 GASCO map (reflecting the network as of end of June 2018, per the report's own text) already draws the Abu Sultan–El Shabab line in GREEN ('Existing P/L'), meaning the physical pipe was already in service roughly three years before the 2021 date on trademanegypt's page. The two facts are reconcilable (e.g., Trademan's 2021 contract could be a valve/materials replacement or rehabilitation on an already-operating line) but are NOT the same claim, and GEM's current single StartMonth1='2021' value reads as if it were the original construction/start date, which the map evidence contradicts. Left unresolved pending a source that dates the original construction.
